subject: Re: Performance SLO / Concurrency qualification + Redwood rate limits
content:
Message 1 (2027-07-10T14:12:00-07:00)
From: Peter Shaw <peter@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah@nimbushealth.com>
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Concurrency qualification

Thanks for the call earlier — helpful to see Redwood's routing + caching approach.

Quick recap of what we need to validate for our integration:
- Latency target: 95th percentile under 200ms for single-turn text-gen (context ~256 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 30 req/s peak across our cluster, with spikes to 120 req/s for short bursts.
- Concurrency: we expect ~250 concurrent active requests during peak; many clients will open long-lived connections (~200ms average response).
- Streaming: client side expects tokens to stream as they are generated (low latency first byte).
- Connection pooling: our service uses 100 connection pools (per region) and reuses HTTP/2 multiplexing.

Can Redwood support a quota of 300 concurrent connections for us at launch and provide a recommended rate-limiting profile? Also please share any guidance on retry/backoff for streaming endpoints.

Thanks,
Peter
VP Product, Acme AI

---
Message 2 (2027-07-10T17:03:00-07:00)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Peter Shaw <peter@acmeai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Concurrency qualification

Peter — great talking earlier. Appreciate the summary; confirming a few follow-ups and next steps.

Recap & clarifying Qs:
- Latency: 200ms P95 for single-turn gen with 256 tokens of context is ambitious but plausible on our low-latency profile. We'll need to validate model choice and quantization. Which model family are you evaluating? (GPT-like open model or 3rd-party vendor?)
- Throughput/spikes: our hosted clusters can sustain 30 req/s easily; bursts to 120 req/s look fine but we should plan for automatic burst capacity or a reserved Dedicated pool if you need strict guarantees.
- Concurrency: you asked for 300 concurrent connections. Our default per-account concurrency quota is 100. We can propose a tiered increase to 300 for launch under a committed usage / reserved capacity agreement.
- Streaming + connection pooling: our streaming endpoints support chunked responses and first-byte latency tuning. For HTTP/2 clients we recommend connection re-use and 1-2 concurrent streams per connection to avoid head-of-line on some proxies.

Action items:
1) Jonas — can you validate the feasibility of a 300 concurrency quota on our hosted side and estimate expected cost delta for Acme under a reserved vs burst policy?
2) Laura — I attached a short template (concurrency_requirements.xlsx) to capture expected qps by region and desired SLA. Peter, please fill and return.
3) Peter — please confirm model (and avg token lengths for responses) so we can do an internal perf run. Also confirm whether you need a hard quota (rejecting beyond limit) or soft throttling with 429 + retry semantics.

I'll put together a short rate-limits proposal (pdf) and send by Monday.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Message 3 (2027-07-11T09:08:00-07:00)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Shaw <peter@acmeai.com>
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Concurrency qualification

Looping in engineering notes from a quick capacity check:

- Short answer: hosted can support a temporary per-account concurrency bump to 300 for a pilot.
- We recommend a phased approach: 100 (default) -> 200 (pilot) -> 300 (production) over 2-4 weeks. That lets us observe tail latency and KV cache hit rates.
- Costing: estimated incremental cost ~ +22% on token/serving unit for sustained 300 concurrency vs default; precise numbers in the attached doc (redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf).
- Rate-limiting profile suggestion:
  * Per-account concurrency hard limit (rejecting with 429) configurable per contract (default 100).
  * Additional soft quota using token-based smoothing: burst window of 60s with 3x baseline QPS allowed then throttle.
  * For streaming endpoints: recommend smaller per-connection stream limits (2-3) to avoid amplification; use retry-after header for 429s.

We can also enable connection-level queueing on Dedicated pools (bounded queue) which keeps P95 stable under spikes.

Jonas
SRE / Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

---
Message 4 (2027-07-12T09:34:00-07:00)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Peter Shaw <peter@acmeai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Concurrency qualification + Redwood rate limits (proposal)

Peter — attaching the proposal and the filled concurrency worksheet. Summary of the recommended plan for launch:

1) Pilot launch (2 weeks): increase account concurrency to 200, enable burst window to 3x baseline QPS, monitor P95 and KV cache hit.
2) Production ramp (after successful pilot): increase to 300 concurrency, move to reserved capacity or a committed Dedicated pool if you need strict latency SLAs.
3) Rate limit semantics: we can offer either hard reject at configured concurrency (429 + Retry-After) or soft throttling with token-bucket smoothing — most customers prefer soft smoothing for streaming UX.

Request: please confirm by EOD Tuesday if Acme wants the pilot bump to 200 and whether you prefer hard rejects or soft throttling. Once confirmed Jonas will provision the quota and I will generate an updated pricing addendum.

Thanks — speaking to legal about a short PILOT MOU for the concurrency bump; will share draft.

Cheers,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

> Attachments: concurrency_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-rate-limits-proposal.pdf (proposal stub)
